issues.display_title: [GoThruMedia/panorra-api-new] Issue #335: Optimize location grouping trigger on AddPostComplete
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 09/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Implementation :

Overview

Decouple location grouping from the synchronous post-publishing flow in the AddPostComplete API handler. The handler should only save raw location data and publish a message to the _location_grouping RabbitMQ queue.

File: src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPostComplete.go

Problem

  • Synchronous spatial calculation inside the publish path adds latency to user notifications and ElasticSearch indexing.
  • Coordinates stored only in the location_post JSON (with empty 0.0 standalone columns) cause failed nearby-group matching, leading to duplicate location slugs.

Scope

  • On action == "publish", publish {post_id} to the {PREFIX}_location_grouping queue.
  • Persist raw location data (incl. place_id, JSON coords) without resolving the group inline.
  • Remove any direct ResolveLocationGroup call from this handler path.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Publishing a post via AddPostComplete returns without waiting on spatial grouping.
  • A message lands on {PREFIX}_location_grouping with the correct post_id.
  • place_id and JSON coordinates are persisted on the post.
  • No duplicate location slug created for posts sharing the same place_id.

Scenario Testing (for tester)

Pre-conditions: Logged-in user with a panorama upload ready; RabbitMQ + LocationGrouping worker running; access to DB and the {PREFIX}_location_grouping queue.

  1. Happy path — publish triggers async grouping
    • Call AddPostComplete with action = "publish" and a valid location (name + place_id + coordinates).
    • Expected: API responds quickly (no wait for spatial calc); a message with the correct post_id appears on {PREFIX}_location_grouping; post row has raw location saved.
  2. Coordinates only in JSON (empty standalone columns)
    • Publish a post where latitude/longitude columns are 0.0 but coords exist in location_post JSON.
    • Expected: post is enqueued; after the worker runs, the post is grouped correctly (NOT measured from 0,0); no new duplicate slug.
  3. Same Place ID → same group
    • Publish two posts with the same place_id but slightly different coordinates.
    • Expected: both land in the same location_group / location_group_slug (no fragmentation).
  4. Draft / non-publish action
    • Call with action != "publish".
    • Expected: NO message published to {PREFIX}_location_grouping; no grouping triggered.
  5. Latency check
    • Compare response time vs. previous synchronous behavior.
    • Expected: publish response no longer blocks on spatial grouping.

Pass criteria: All acceptance-criteria boxes verified; no duplicate slug for identical place_id; queue message confirmed.

Reference

docs/brainstorm/OPTIMIZE_LOCATION_GROUPING.md

issues.display_title: [GoThruMedia/panorra-api-new] Issue #338: Worker: Location Grouping (async spatial + place_id matching)
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 09/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Implementation :

Overview

Dedicated asynchronous worker that handles all spatial and grouping logic off the post-publishing critical path, with improved accuracy via Google Place ID matching.

File: src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping.go Queue: {PREFIX}_location_grouping

Problem

  • Spatial grouping must run async to keep publishing fast.
  • Coordinate drift between the location_post JSON and standalone latitude/longitude columns causes slug fragmentation (distance computed from 0,0 when columns are empty).
  • Minor coordinate variations for the same physical location can wrongly trigger new group creation.

Scope

  • Consume {PREFIX}_location_grouping; fetch the post's location data by post_id.
  • ResolveLocationGroup logic:
    • Place ID match: same Google place_id → same group, regardless of coordinate drift or column status.
    • Empty-column fallback: when standalone coords are 0, default to exact name matching within the same vicinity (prevents slug fragmentation).
    • Haversine 15km as secondary check for custom locations without a place_id.
  • JSON-to-column sync: extract latitude/longitude from location_post JSON and update the posts columns.
  • Update location_group + location_group_slug on the post.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Posts sharing the same place_id are assigned to the same group.
  • Empty coordinate columns no longer match against 0,0.
  • latitude/longitude are backfilled to the posts columns from JSON.
  • Slug fragmentation for identical locations is eliminated.

Scenario Testing (for tester)

Pre-conditions: Worker process running and consuming {PREFIX}_location_grouping; ability to publish test messages and inspect the posts table.

  1. Place ID match grouping
    • Enqueue two post_ids with the same place_id but coords ~hundreds of meters apart.
    • Expected: both get the SAME location_group + location_group_slug.
  2. Empty standalone columns + JSON coords
    • Enqueue a post with latitude/longitude = 0.0 and valid coords in location_post JSON.
    • Expected: worker syncs coords from JSON into the columns; grouping uses real coords, not 0,0.
  3. Exact name fallback (no usable coords)
    • Enqueue a post with empty coords but a name matching an existing nearby group.
    • Expected: assigned to the existing group (no new slug).
  4. Haversine 15km secondary check (custom location, no place_id)
    • Enqueue two posts without place_id: one within 15km of an existing group, one beyond 15km.
    • Expected: the near one joins the existing group; the far one creates a new group.
  5. New unique slug creation
    • Enqueue a genuinely new location.
    • Expected: a new, unique location_group_slug is generated.
  6. Idempotency / re-processing
    • Re-enqueue the same post_id.
    • Expected: stable group assignment (no duplicate group, no slug churn).
  7. Malformed / missing post
    • Enqueue a non-existent post_id or malformed payload.
    • Expected: worker handles gracefully (logs + skips/nacks), does not crash or block the queue.

Pass criteria: All acceptance criteria verified; DB shows correct group/slug + backfilled coords; queue keeps draining without stalls.

Reference

docs/brainstorm/OPTIMIZE_LOCATION_GROUPING.md. Related logic: src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/LocationGrouping.go.

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 09/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Implementation :

Overview

Refactor the PostComplete worker to remove synchronous location grouping. It should save raw location data only and delegate grouping to the dedicated _location_grouping worker.

File: src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go Queue consumed: {PREFIX}_add_post_complete

Problem

  • PostComplete currently runs ResolveLocationGroup synchronously, slowing user notifications and ElasticSearch indexing.

Scope

  • Remove the synchronous ResolveLocationGroup call from PostComplete.
  • Save raw location data and publish {post_id} to the {PREFIX}_location_grouping queue for published posts.
  • Confirm the push-notification / ElasticSearch / Maps Panorra flow no longer blocks on spatial calculation.

Acceptance Criteria

  • PostComplete no longer calls ResolveLocationGroup inline.
  • Grouping is handled by the dedicated _location_grouping worker.
  • Post-publish latency is reduced (notifications/ES indexing fire without waiting on grouping).
  • No regression in notifications, ElasticSearch sync, or Maps Panorra sync.

Scenario Testing (for tester)

Pre-conditions: PostComplete worker + LocationGrouping worker both running; Redis, ElasticSearch, push-notification, and Maps Panorra integrations available; DB + queue access.

  1. End-to-end publish flow
    • Publish a post so a message hits {PREFIX}_add_post_complete.
    • Expected: PostComplete finalizes the post (thumbnail, description, animation, location saved), sends push notification, syncs ES + Maps Panorra — WITHOUT computing the location group itself.
  2. Grouping delegated downstream
    • After step 1, inspect {PREFIX}_location_grouping.
    • Expected: a message with the correct post_id was published; the LocationGrouping worker later sets location_group + location_group_slug.
  3. No inline grouping
    • Verify via logs/code path that ResolveLocationGroup is NOT invoked inside PostComplete.
    • Expected: no synchronous spatial calculation in this worker.
  4. Notifications / ES not blocked
    • Temporarily stop the LocationGrouping worker, then publish a post.
    • Expected: push notification + ES indexing still complete promptly; grouping simply pends until the worker resumes.
  5. Latency regression check
    • Measure PostComplete processing time before vs after.
    • Expected: reduced/no spatial-calc time in the critical path.
  6. No regression
    • Verify thumbnail, description, animation, location data, push notification, ES doc, and Maps Panorra entry are all correct.

Pass criteria: All acceptance criteria verified; grouping happens only via the dedicated worker; no regression in notifications/ES/Maps.

Reference

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 09/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Implementation :

Objective

Block add/remove bookmark operations on bookmark folders where is_published = true, to maintain data integrity.

API

  • File: src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/AddBookmark.go

Tasks

  • Use shared helper CheckFolderPublished(c *fiber.Ctx, qSid string, sid string, userId string) (FolderStatus, bool) in src/Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions/BookmarkFunctions.go (create it if not present)
    • Queries folder_bookmark table
    • Returns 409 Conflict if folder not found
    • Returns 403 Forbidden with message "Activity not allowed for published folder" if is_published = true
  • Invoke the helper in AddBookmark.go and block add/remove when the folder is published

How to test

  1. Identify a bookmark folder with is_published = true.
  2. Attempt to add a bookmark to this folder via the AddBookmark API.
  3. Expected: 403 Forbidden with message "Activity not allowed for published folder".

Verification

  • go build passes on affected package
  • Returns consistent 403 + message

Testing Scenario (for QA)

Preconditions

  • Valid authenticated user with access to bookmark folders.
  • At least one folder with is_published = true (Folder A) and one with is_published = false (Folder B).
#ScenarioStepsExpected Result
TC-1Add bookmark to a published folderCall AddBookmark API targeting Folder A403 Forbidden, body message "Activity not allowed for published folder". Bookmark is NOT added.
TC-2Remove bookmark from a published folderCall AddBookmark/remove API targeting Folder A403 Forbidden, message "Activity not allowed for published folder". Bookmark is NOT removed.
TC-3Add bookmark to an unpublished folderCall AddBookmark API targeting Folder BSuccess (normal 200/expected response). Bookmark added correctly.
TC-4Remove bookmark from an unpublished folderCall remove on Folder BSuccess. Bookmark removed correctly.
TC-5Target a non-existent folderCall AddBookmark with an invalid/unknown folder id409 Conflict.
TC-6RegressionConfirm pre-existing AddBookmark behavior on unpublished folders is unchangedNo regressions in normal add/remove flow.

Pass criteria: TC-1, TC-2 return 403 with the exact message; TC-3, TC-4 succeed; TC-5 returns 409; no regressions.

Source: docs/brainstorm/2026-06-09-add-bookmark-validation.md

issues.display_title: [GoThruMedia/panorra-api-go] Issue #410: Implement GET /affiliate/list endpoint (own-user affiliate links)
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 09/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Base Route :

GET /affiliate/list

Header :

  • Authorization
  • ec (ec=true for pwa)

Param :

  • limit
  • page

Example change :

GET /affiliate/list?limit=2&page=1

Objective

Add a new authenticated endpoint GET /affiliate/list that returns the logged-in user's own affiliate rows straight from the affiliate table (all columns, no join), newest first, paginated, with the project's standard ec encrypted-response support.

Source of truth: docs/brainstorming/2026-06-04-affiliate-list-plugin-executor-brainstorm.md and docs/analysis/AFFILIATE_LIST_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md. Stack: Go + Fiber v2 + GORM, flat Action → Controller → Route architecture.

Acceptance criteria

  • go build ./... succeeds.
  • GET /affiliate/list with a user JWT → 200 + data.data_affiliate[] + data.total.
  • A user with no affiliates → 200, data_affiliate: [], total: 0 (never null).
  • viewer / no token → 401.
  • ec: true header → encrypted { messages, cry, ls }; ec:true + sl=true → V1 variant.
  • A client can never read another user's affiliates (scope is server-derived).

Locked decisions

  • D1 Own-user only: WHERE affiliate.user_id = <caller>. No sid/username param.
  • D2 Direct table read, NO JOIN. category_id returned as-is (integer); do not join affiliate_categories.
  • D3 Role user only. Reject viewer/others with 401.
  • D4 Response fields = affiliate columns: id, user_id, category_id, title, url, description, cta_text, created_at, updated_at.
  • D5 Order created_at DESC; pagination page(1)/limit(20)/offset.
  • D6 ec supports both branches (sl=true → …V1, else default cry).

Implementation steps

  1. Model — create src/Models/AffiliateModel.go (AffiliateListItem struct).
  2. Action — create src/Action/V1/Affiliate/ListAffiliate.go (role check, pagination, user resolve, count, fetch, ec response).
  3. Controller — create src/Controllers/V1/AffiliateControllers.go.
  4. Routes — create src/Routes/V1/AffiliateRoutes.go and register registerAffiliateRoutes(http) in src/Routes/V1/Routes.go after registerPlacesRoutes(http).
  5. Auth — no change; /affiliate/list is auth-protected via not being in IgnoreAuthPath.
  6. Build & smoke test — go build ./..., go vet, then curl smoke tests (happy path, pagination, encrypted, encrypted V1, unauthorized=401).

Out of scope

  • Create / edit / delete affiliate (other project).
  • Joining affiliate_categories / resolving category name.
  • Any external view, new table, or schema migration.
  • Profile-scoped reads, click tracking, URL enrichment.

Generated from the brainstorming brief on the brainstorm branch.

issues.display_title: [GoThruMedia/panorra-api-new] Issue #343: Health Check Coverage Expansion for /check-connection
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Implementation :

Overview

Upgrade the /check-connection endpoint to provide a comprehensive overview of system health. It now monitors not only core infrastructure (Database, Redis, etc.) but also essential third-party APIs and internal microservices used throughout the Panorra API.

Subtasks

New services to monitor

  • Add RabbitMQ Toronto (secondary message broker for data synchronization) to the health check suite
  • Add Centrifugo connectivity check (ENDPOINT_CENTRIFUGO)
  • Add SMTP server reachability check (SMTP_HOST / SMTP_PORT)
  • Add Maps API availability check (API_MAPS)
  • Add GoThru API availability check (API_GOTHRU)

Architectural optimizations

  • Reuse RabbitMQ singleton connection (RabbitMQ.GetConnection()) instead of spawning new TCP handshakes per request
  • Add fail-safe fallback to a temporary dial when the singleton connection is closed/uninitialized
  • Enforce a strict 5-second timeout on all HTTP-based checks (Centrifugo, Maps, GoThru)
  • Treat any HTTP status code < 500 as "Up" so auth-protected services (401/403) report as reachable

Endpoint

  • Aggregate all new services into the /check-connection GET response (public, no auth)

Endpoint Specification

URL: /check-connection · Method: GET · Auth: None (publicly accessible for monitoring tools)

Sample Response

{
  "status": "ok",
  "services": {
    "database": "up",
    "redis": "up",
    "elasticsearch": "up",
    "rabbitmq": "up",
    "minio": "up",
    "rabbitmq_toronto": "up",
    "centrifugo": "up",
    "smtp": "up",
    "maps_api": "up",
    "gothru_api": "up"
  }
}

Affected Files

  • src/Utils/Functions/CheckConnection/CheckConnection.go — logic implementation for all health checks
  • src/Routes/V1/Routes.go — route definition and result aggregation

Source: docs/brainstorm/HEALTH_CHECK_UPDATES.md

🧪 Scenario Testing (For Tester)

Endpoint under test: GET /check-connection (public, no auth required)

TC-01 — Happy path: all services reachable

  • Steps: Ensure all infra/third-party services are running, then call GET /check-connection.
  • Expected: HTTP 200; status = "ok"; every service in services reports "up" (database, redis, elasticsearch, rabbitmq, minio, rabbitmq_toronto, centrifugo, smtp, maps_api, gothru_api).

TC-02 — New services present in response

  • Steps: Call the endpoint and inspect the services object.
  • Expected: The five new keys exist: rabbitmq_toronto, centrifugo, smtp, maps_api, gothru_api.

TC-03 — Service down is detected

  • Steps: Stop one service (e.g. Centrifugo / SMTP / Maps), then call the endpoint.
  • Expected: That service reports "down" (or not "up"); endpoint still returns a response without hanging; overall status reflects degradation.

TC-04 — 5-second timeout enforced (HTTP checks)

  • Steps: Make an HTTP-checked service (Centrifugo, Maps, GoThru) unresponsive/slow (>5s), then call the endpoint.
  • Expected: The endpoint responds in ~5s for that check (does not hang indefinitely); the slow service reports "down".

TC-05 — Auth-protected service reported reachable

  • Steps: Point an HTTP check at a service that returns 401/403 (any status < 500).
  • Expected: Service is reported as "up" (reachable), not "down".

TC-06 — RabbitMQ singleton reuse

  • Steps: With RabbitMQ singleton connection already established, call the endpoint multiple times in succession.
  • Expected: Existing RabbitMQ.GetConnection() is reused (no new TCP handshake per request); rabbitmq reports "up".

TC-07 — RabbitMQ fail-safe fallback

issues.display_title: [GoThruMedia/panorra-api-new] Issue #349: Implement username deduplication in MentionPost worker
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Overview

Implement a duplicate-username elimination (deduplication) layer for mention-based notifications inside the Background Worker (src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost.go).

When a user is mentioned more than once in a single context (post or comment) — e.g. "ipeb, lundara, ipeb" — the system must send only one notification and create only one mention record per unique user.

Problem Statement

Previously every entry in the comma-separated recipientUsername string was processed, causing duplicate DB entries and multiple push notifications to the same user for the same event.

Design Decision: Worker-Side Processing

Deduplication is performed in the Background Worker (not the API) to keep API response time low and consistent, align with the existing asynchronous RabbitMQ delivery flow, and centralize username→userID resolution + block-list checks in one place right before notification logic.

Implementation Details

In src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost.go, on receiving a mention payload:

  1. Split the recipientUsername comma-separated string into a raw slice.
  2. Deduplicate using a map[string]bool to track seen usernames.
  3. Sanitize each username by trimming whitespace; skip empty entries.
  4. Rebuild a unique slice used for all subsequent DB lookups and notification broadcasts.
rawMentions := strings.Split(recipientUsername, ",")
uniqueMap := make(map[string]bool)
arrayMentions := []string{}
for _, m := range rawMentions {
    m = strings.TrimSpace(m)
    if m != "" && !uniqueMap[m] {
        uniqueMap[m] = true
        arrayMentions = append(arrayMentions, m)
    }
}

Acceptance Criteria

  • Duplicate usernames in a single mention event produce exactly one notification per unique user.
  • Whitespace is trimmed; empty entries (trailing/double commas) are skipped.
  • Only unique mention records are written to the database.
  • Block-list and username→userID resolution still work correctly after dedup.
  • API response time remains unaffected (dedup happens worker-side).

🧪 Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Scenario 1 — Duplicate elimination

  1. Create a post/comment mentioning the same user multiple times: "ipeb, lundara, ipeb".
  2. Verify ipeb receives only ONE notification (not two).
  3. Verify lundara still receives their notification normally.
  4. Check the DB — confirm only one mention record per unique user per event.
  • Expected: No duplicate DB entries, no duplicate push notifications.

Scenario 2 — Whitespace & empty-entry sanitization

  1. Submit mentions with irregular spacing/commas: " ipeb , lundara , , ipeb,".
  2. Verify only ipeb and lundara are processed (no empty/blank recipients).
  3. Verify " ipeb" and "ipeb" are treated as the same user (trim works).
  • Expected: Exactly 2 unique notifications; no errors from empty strings.

Scenario 3 — Block-list & resolution integrity

  1. Mention a user who has blocked the author, multiple times in one event.
  2. Verify the block is honored — no notification is sent to that user.
  3. Mention a mix of valid, duplicate, and blocked users in one event.
  • Expected: Each valid unique user gets exactly one notification; blocked users get none.

Scenario 4 — Regression & performance (redundant input)

  1. Submit a post with a large mention list containing many duplicates (e.g. 50 entries, 5 unique).
  2. Measure API response time — should remain low/consistent (dedup is worker-side).
  3. Verify only 5 notifications and 5 DB records result.
  • Expected: Stable API latency, correct dedup, no DB query explosion.

Source: docs/brainstorm/2026-06-11-duplicate-mention-elimination.md

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.views_timeline_post AS
SELECT
    posts.category_id, posts.created_at, posts.animation, posts.animation_filter, posts.description, posts.slug, posts.little_planet, posts.little_planet_filter, posts.location_post, posts.location_name, posts.panorama, posts.thumbnail, posts.panorama_preview, posts.post_type, posts.panorama_quality, posts.pending, posts.score_mostpopular, posts.score_timeline, posts.user_id, users.avatar, users.fullname, users.username, users.encrypt,
    CASE WHEN broadcast.post_id IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END AS potd,
    CASE WHEN broadcast.post_id IS NOT NULL THEN json_build_object('title', broadcast.title, 'message', broadcast.messages) ELSE NULL END AS broadcast_data,
    posts.is_processing, posts.visibility,
    (SELECT jsonb_build_object(
        'id',          a.id,
        'title',       a.title,
        'url',         a.url,
        'description', a.description,
        'cta_text',    a.cta_text,
        'category_id', a.category_id
      ) FROM panorra_dev.public.affiliate a WHERE a.id = posts.affiliate_id) AS affiliate,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT jsonb_agg(
               jsonb_build_object(
                 'sequence',    ph.sequence,
                 'type',        ph.type,
                 'coordinates', ph.coordinates,
                 'data',        ph.data
               ) ORDER BY ph.sequence ASC
             )
      FROM panorra_dev.public.post_hotspots ph
      WHERE ph.post_id = posts.id
    ), '[]'::jsonb) AS hotspot
FROM panorra_dev.public.posts
LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.users ON users.id = posts.user_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (post_id) post_id, title, messages FROM panorra_dev.public.broadcast ORDER BY post_id, created_at DESC) AS broadcast ON broadcast.post_id = posts.id
WHERE ((posts.is_publish = true) AND (posts.banned = false)) AND (users.banned = false)
GROUP BY
    posts.category_id, posts.created_at, posts.animation, posts.animation_filter, posts.description, posts.slug, posts.little_planet, posts.little_planet_filter, posts.location_post, posts.location_name, posts.panorama, posts.thumbnail, posts.panorama_preview, posts.post_type, posts.panorama_quality, posts.pending, posts.score_mostpopular, posts.score_timeline, posts.user_id, users.avatar, users.fullname, users.username, users.encrypt, broadcast.post_id, broadcast.messages, broadcast.title, posts.is_processing, posts.visibility,
    posts.affiliate_id, posts.id;

Context: Part of the Detail Post enhancement to add data.posts.affiliate and data.posts.hotspot. See docs/brainstorm/DETAIL_POST_AFFILIATE_HOTSPOT_BRAINSTORM.md.

Add two new columns to views_timeline_post (assuming posts alias p):

  • affiliate (jsonb) via LEFT JOIN affiliate a ON a.id = p.affiliate_id, returning id, title, url, description, cta_text, category_id; NULL when no affiliate.
  • hotspot (jsonb array) via a scalar subquery to post_hotspots ordered by sequence ASC, wrapped in COALESCE(..., '[]'). Each item: sequence, type, coordinates, data.

A scalar subquery is used (NOT JOIN ... GROUP BY) so the ~17 endpoints sharing this view are not burdened with aggregation.

-- affiliate
CASE WHEN a.id IS NULL THEN NULL
ELSE jsonb_build_object('id',a.id,'title',a.title,'url',a.url,
  'description',a.description,'cta_text',a.cta_text,'category_id',a.category_id)
END AS affiliate,
-- hotspot
COALESCE((
  SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('sequence',ph.sequence,'type',ph.type,
    'coordinates',ph.coordinates,'data',ph.data) ORDER BY ph.sequence ASC)
  FROM post_hotspots ph WHERE ph.post_id = p.id
), '[]'::jsonb) AS hotspot

Acceptance Criteria:

  • affiliate column returns the agreed 6 fields, or NULL.
  • hotspot column returns an ordered array, or [].

  4. Query a post with no hotspots → hotspot equals [] (not null).

📌 Context

Detail Draft Post (GET /draft-detail/:sid, src/Action/V1/Posts/DetailDraftPost.go) must expose two new datasets without changing any existing response field:

Fields appear at data.draft.* (and data.detail_draft.* when ?sl=true). No DB migration — the endpoint queries the posts table directly (not the views_timeline_post view).

Ref: docs/brainstorm/DETAIL_DRAFT_POST_AFFILIATE_HOTSPOT_BRAINSTORM.md

  • Affiliate *postgres.Jsonb json:"affiliate" — pointer → empty becomes null.
  • Hotspot postgres.Jsonb json:"hotspot" gorm:"type:jsonb;default:'[]'" — empty becomes [].

  • LEFT JOIN affiliate ON affiliate.id = posts.affiliate_id.
  • Affiliate CASE ... jsonb_build_object('id','title','url','description','cta_text','category_id') → NULL when none.
  • Hotspot scalar subquery COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('sequence','type','coordinates','data') ORDER BY ph.sequence ASC), '[]'::jsonb) from post_hotspots where ph.post_id = posts.id.
  • Covers both draft and detail_draft (sl=true) paths automatically.
